rejected: effective but not ours to set, an MCP server is launched by its client

limitations: Resident size is read from /proc/self/statm, so the benchmark reports no resident metric on darwin and the comparison exists only on Linux.

The first samples taken during this investigation ran on a cold page cache and were 2.7-3.3 s per build; every number here is warm. An allocator strategy cannot be timed against a cold read of a 189 MB file.
The four builds happen in one process, which is what a server does across published generations. A single build in a fresh process does not show the growth.
The graph is a real corpus, not a generated one: a synthetic corpus with few distinct strings measures the interner rather than the string volume a real scan decodes.
